record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: For a positive integer n, let CP_n be the cone of real symmetric n x n completely positive matrices, meaning matrices A that can be written as A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative matrix B. Is the decision problem that takes a real symmetric n x n matrix A as input and asks whether A is in CP_n an NP-complete problem?

evidence.quote: It is open whether checking membership in CPn is also NP-complete.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $\mathrm{CP}_n$ denote the cone of real symmetric $n\times n$ completely positive matrices, that is, the set of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices $A$ admitting a factorization $A = BB^T$ for some (rectangular) entrywise nonnegative real matrix $B$. Consider the following decision problem: given a real symmetric $n\times n$ matrix $A$ with rational entries (encoded in the usual binary representation), decide whether $A \in \mathrm{CP}_n$. Is this decision problem NP-complete?
artifact.status_search_result: Membership in the completely positive cone is known to be NP-hard (Dickinson–Gijben and related work), but whether it lies in NP — and hence is NP-complete — remains open. No source located establishes containment in NP or a stronger hardness result that would resolve NP-completeness.

status_evidence.title: On the computational complexity of membership problems for the completely positive cone and its dual
status_evidence.snippet: The strong membership problem for the completely positive cone is shown to be NP-hard; NP-completeness is not established.
status_evidence.claim: CP membership is NP-hard, but no proof of NP-completeness is given.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices (ELA)
status_evidence.snippet: It is open whether checking membership in CPn is also NP-complete.
status_evidence.claim: The NP-completeness question for CP_n membership is explicitly listed as open.
